turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’m here for my annual well-check, and I’ve noticed a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. It hasn’t been tender or painful.

How long has the rough, scaly plaque on your left hand been there?
How long has the rough, scaly plaque on your left hand been there?
Patient: It’s been there for a few months now, maybe around three to four months. It hasn’t been painful or tender, just a persistent rough, scaly spot on the left dorsal hand.
Has it changed over time—such as getting larger, thicker, bleeding, crusting, or ulcerating?
Patient: I think it’s slowly gotten a bit larger and thicker, but it hasn’t been bleeding or ulcerating—no crusting or open sore.
Do you get a lot of sun exposure on your hands, or have you had significant lifetime sun exposure, like outdoor work or frequent sunburns?

Patient: Yes, I do spend time outdoors and I enjoy walking and sunbathing, so I’d say I’ve had quite a bit of sun exposure over the years. I don’t recall frequent sunburns, but my hands are often out in the sun.
Have you noticed any similar rough spots elsewhere, or do you have a history of skin cancer or precancerous lesions?
Patient: I haven’t noticed similar rough spots anywhere else, and I don’t have a personal history of skin cancer or any precancerous lesions that I know of.
[DDX] Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma in situ (Bowen disease), invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, irritated seborrheic keratosis, superficial basal cell carcinoma
